# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 108 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 108 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_108_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 25

**1** After he had finished the similitude of the tower with me, I asked him about the round stones that were taken from the deep and fitted into the tower, and about those who were fitted in after the round ones had been cut. **2** And he said to me: "I have said before that all these will be found useful to the building. And so also these round stones that were taken from the deep — these had to be placed in the building. **3** But first they had to be cut in order to fit in with the others; for this reason they were delayed. **4** But I am pleased that they repented after they heard my words; for this reason they were cut and placed in the building. **5** But those who did not repent — these died, for those who were cut and thrown away by the stone-cutters died; and those who are still living and are to be cut — if they are cut, they shall live. But if they do not repent they shall die." **6** "But, Lord," I said, "why do some of them repent when they hear these things, and others do not repent?" **7** "Those who do not have goodness in them," he said, "do not repent, because the hardness of their heart and the wicked desires they have dried up the goodness in them; but those who have goodness in them repent. **8** Now because good understanding dwells in the hearts of those who repent, they repented quickly — and so their goodness was not dried up." **9** I asked him further about the cracked ones, for the cracks were in them. "Why were these cracked? Were they cracked from the beginning?" **10** "No," he said, "the cracks in them came from afterwards; for their repentance was not made with the whole heart; therefore they remain cracked and not sound." **11** "But those who repent with their whole heart — can they become sound?" "Yes," he said, "if they repent with their whole heart."

---

*EMET: the distinction between those who repent quickly (goodness not dried up) and those who cannot (hardness dried out the goodness) is a sophisticated moral psychology.*
